text: That afternoon: Holmes tells Miss Stoner to lock herself up to-night and asks to be taken to the rooms
why: Holmes tells Helen to lock herself in to-night and asks to be taken at once to the rooms, both stated in ¶131, which is the afternoon trip set up in ¶¶76-82.

text: Will Helen Stoner suffer for having been traced? — he turns violent and she has to be taken to her aunt's at Harrow
id: q.helen_after=he turns violent and she has to be taken to her aunt's at Harrow
why: Helen has said she is afraid and that he has followed her (¶128-130), and Holmes says 'If he is violent, we shall take you away to your aunt's at Harrow' (¶131). The label frames this as a possibility, which the story gives reason to consider.

text: Will locking her door keep Helen safe to-night?
why: A plain question. Helen has said she is in danger and Holmes has just advised locking herself in, so the question is one the story gives reason to raise.

text: Will locking her door keep Helen safe to-night? — yes: a locked door will keep him out
id: q.lock_safe=yes: a locked door will keep him out
why: A possibility the story gives reason to consider. Holmes has just advised locking the door, and Julia's locked door is mentioned earlier (¶44), so a locked door being protective is a live possibility.

text: Will locking her door keep Helen safe to-night? — no: whatever reached Julia got past a locked door
id: q.lock_safe=no: whatever reached Julia got past a locked door
why: A possibility the story gives reason to consider. Julia's death happened behind a door that was fastened on the inner side (¶56), and the mystery of how something reached her in that room is set up, so a reader can consider that a locked door was passed.

text: Will locking her door keep Helen safe to-night? — it will not be put to the test: nothing will be tried to-night
